newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean central bank says money market stable.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean central bank says money market stable.

text.p: South Korea's central bank governor Lee Kyung-shick said on Saturday the local money market remained stable despite the financial failure of Hanbo Steel Co .
Lee said the Bank of Korea had taken steps to avoid a credit crunch by managing money supply flexibly.

Lee said the impact from the Hanbo failure was exaggerated in some international financial markets, including those in Tokyo and that some overseas branches of South Korean banks faced difficulty in raising funds.
"Overseas borrowing conditions worsened slightly for some banks but overall it is not a worrying level," Lee told a news conference.

He said the interest rate for short-term loans applied to South Korean banks on Thursday was 0.32 percentage points above the London Interbank Offered Rate, about 0.05 percentage points higher than before the Hanbo failure.
Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, defaulted on debt repayments last week after piling up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.
The government said on Friday it will take steps to keep Hanbo Steel running. The company is the flagship of the Hanbo Group, South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate.
Lee said creditor banks have agreed to support the completion of Hanbo Steel's new mill being built in the southwestern city of Tangjin.
Lee said some South Korean banks would soon sell foreign-currency-denominated securites and other assets to generate funds to support overseas branches facing cash shortage.
"I think this situation will be resolved soon," Lee said.
"The Bank of Korea will monitor the trend of overseas short-term borrowings and foreign currency liquidity. We plan to take proper steps if necessary," he said, without elaborating.
The central bank has bought back Monetary Stabilisation Bonds before maturity and resorted to repurchase arrangements to release 3.6 trillion won since last week.
